# 2.11.0

Route resolution on the RPC server no longer reaches anything the schema never indexed.

- `PIPE` steps now pass the same `isSafeKey` filter as the path in `ref`, and the whole chain is
  validated before any stage runs. Previously steps were unfiltered: `{type:'get',prop:'constructor'}`
  turned the bound method into `Function`, and two further `call` steps executed arbitrary source
  inside the server process — reachable by any client past the `authed` gate, which without an
  `auth` option is every client. Malformed steps (not an object, unknown `type`, non-string `prop`,
  non-array `args`) are refused the same way instead of being silently skipped.
- The string-path fallback resolves own members only. It used `in`, which walks the prototype
  chain, while `routeMap` and the strict schema are built from `Object.keys`. Every
  `Object.prototype` member (`toString`, `hasOwnProperty`, `__defineGetter__`, …) and every
  prototype method of a class-shaped facade was therefore callable without ever being advertised.
  **Behavior change:** a facade that relied on prototype methods being reachable must move them to
  own members; the schema never listed them, so no client could have discovered them from it.
  A proxy-backed surface whose members exist only in `has`/`get` traps now requires `noStrict(...)`;
  a proxy reached *through* a marked node needs no mark of its own, since the flag latches for the
  rest of the path. Marking also makes the node visible to the client as `"dynamic"`, which is what
  lets the strict lane descend into it — an unmarked empty node renders as `{}` and was never
  addressable from the schema in the first place.
- `doc/RPC-AUTH.md` Rule 3 now states both rules; its previous claim that the fallback "finds a
  non-function and rejects" was true only for facades whose prototype is `Object.prototype`.
- New real-socket oracle `oracle/realsocket/pipe-guard.spec.ts` covers both guards over genuine
  WebSocket transport, driving raw `Pkt.PIPE` / `Pkt.CALL` frames the official client cannot build,
  and proves a rejected chain executes no stage. It also pins two measured transport facts: the
  default socket.io parser drops the connection at the 11th binary attachment in one packet, and
  `socket.io-msgpack-parser` carries 200 but returns a `Uint8Array` as a bare `ArrayBuffer`.
